Publishing data (special rights)

Source: vignettes/writing-data.Rmd
writing-data.Rmd
library(soilhub)

Besides reading, the hub accepts new data: values you computed from the soil data (a soil organic carbon stock, a soil-health score), and whole new source datasets. Writing is reserved to accounts with special rights. This guide lists every step and the right it needs. The writing calls are not run in this guide (they would change the database); the reads at the end were recorded from the Global Soil Data Hub API in October 2026.

Which rights do I need?

Right Who has it What it allows
soil:summary readers catalog, counts, summaries
soil:read readers reading data, exports, soil_resolve_targets()
soil:publish publishers runs, publishing values and scores, source datasets, jobs
soil:admin administrators new variables, products and versions, country refresh

The steps of this guide need:

Step Function Right
1. Register a variable soil_register_variable() soil:admin
2. Register a product and a version soil_product(), soil_product_version() soil:admin
3. Open a run soil_run_open() soil:publish
4. Find the target ids soil_resolve_targets() soil:read
5. Publish the values soil_publish_values() soil:publish
6. Close the run soil_run_complete(), soil_run_fail() soil:publish
7. Read them back soil_values(), soil_values_summary() soil:read, soil:summary
Soil-health scores soil_publish_health() soil:publish
Follow a job soil_job(), soil_job_wait(), soil_job_cancel() soil:publish
A new source dataset soil_publish_source() soil:publish

Check your own rights with soil_whoami() (sign in first with soil <- soil_connect()):

me <- soil_whoami(soil)
me$can
#> summary    read publish   admin
#>    TRUE    TRUE   FALSE   FALSE

If a right is missing, the function stops before sending anything, with a message like this one:

Error: `soil_register_variable()` needs the right `soil:admin`; your session has `soil:summary`, `soil:read`.

Ask the administrator of the hub for the right; nothing was written.

The words of publishing

  • A variable is a property you publish (for example soil_health_physical_score). It must be registered once.
  • A product is the method that computes it (your model), and a version of the product is one fixed release of that method, with the checksum of its code.
  • A run is one execution of a version: every value published belongs to a run, so anybody can see how it was obtained.
  • A target is what a value describes: a feature, a profile, a component or a horizon of the hub, by its id.
  • An idempotency key is a name you choose for each operation (for example "run-kenya-2026-10"). If the same operation is sent twice (a network problem, a script run again), the server recognises the key and does not do it twice.

1. Register the variable (soil:admin) 

soil_register_variable(
  soil,
  variable_code = "soil_health_physical_score",
  name = "Soil health, physical score",
  domain_code = "soil",
  value_type = "numeric",
  measurement_kind_code = "derived",
  allowed_target_levels = "horizon",
  idempotency_key = "var-soil-health-physical-v1"
)

With validate_only = TRUE the server only checks the definition and registers nothing.

2. Register the product and its version (soil:admin)

The product once:

soil_product(soil, "soil_health_fuzzy", "Soil health (fuzzy model)", "horizon")

Then one version per release of your method. The checksum identifies the exact code of the model (here the file model.R):

checksum <- as.character(openssl::sha256(file("model.R")))
version <- soil_product_version(
  soil, "soil_health_fuzzy", "v1.0.0",
  algorithm_checksum = checksum,
  variables = data.frame(variable_code = "soil_health_physical_score",
                         target_levels = "horizon")
)
version$product_version_id

Keep the product_version_id: the next steps need it.

3. Open a run (soil:publish) 

run <- soil_run_open(soil, version$product_version_id, "run-kenya-2026-10")
run$run_id

4. Find the ids of the targets (soil:read)

Your values describe horizons (or profiles, features) of the hub. If you know them by their source identifiers, soil_resolve_targets() gives their ids in the hub:

keys <- data.frame(provider_code = "isric", dataset_code = "wosis_points",
                   release_code = "legacy_materialized", target_level = "profile",
                   source_record_id = c("101", "102"))
ids <- soil_resolve_targets(soil, keys)
ids$target_id

If you read the data with soil_observations(), the ids are already in the columns feature_id, profile_id, component_id and horizon_id.

5. Publish the values (soil:publish)

One row per value, with at least the variable, the target level, the target id and the value:

values <- data.frame(
  variable_code = "soil_health_physical_score",
  target_level = "horizon",
  target_id = c("4fa5fbe3-8fd4-4fb1-94cf-d07963eb50f7",
                "9d55ca7b-e031-427c-8afd-dc2b3b40f8a5"),
  value = c(72.5, 64.0)
)
receipt <- soil_publish_values(soil, run$run_id, values, "values-kenya-2026-10")
receipt$published_count

The server first validates the values, then publishes them. Up to 10,000 rows are sent in one request; more rows are sent as a file (NDJSON) and processed as a job, which the function follows until it ends.

6. Close the run (soil:publish)

When everything is published, close the run as completed; if something went wrong, close it as failed:

soil_run_complete(soil, run$run_id)
# or: soil_run_fail(soil, run$run_id, diagnostics = list(reason = "input error"))

7. Read the values back

Published values can be read by every user with soil:read. These two calls were run against the hub: soil_values() returns the published values,

published <- soil_values(soil, max_rows = 5)
published[, c("variable_code", "target_level", "dataset_code", "value", "value_status", "run_id")]
#> # soilhub values table: 4 rows | hurl_profiles, soter_profiles
#> # no API warnings (soil_warnings), cite with soil_citations()
#>   variable_code target_level   dataset_code value value_status run_id
#> 1         ph_aq      horizon  hurl_profiles   6.5    published     20
#> 2         ph_aq      horizon soter_profiles   6.5    published      3
#> 3         ph_aq      horizon soter_profiles   6.5    published      9
#> 4         ph_aq      horizon soter_profiles   6.5    published     19

and soil_values_summary() counts them (right soil:summary):

soil_values_summary(soil)
#> # soilhub values summary: 4 values on 2 features, 1 variable(s)
#> 
#> By dataset:
#>         dataset    provider value_count feature_count variable_count
#>   hurl_profiles hurl_source           1             1              1
#>  soter_profiles       isric           3             1              1
#> 
#> By target level: horizon 4
#> 
#> By status: published 4

At the time of recording, four test values of pH (ph_aq, 6.5) were published on horizons of two datasets, by four different runs.

Soil-health scores (soil:publish)

Scores of a soil-health model are published like values, with their category, class and the details of the fuzzy model:

scores <- data.frame(
  horizon_id = "4fa5fbe3-8fd4-4fb1-94cf-d07963eb50f7",
  release_id = 12L,
  category_code = "physical",
  score_status = "scored",
  score = 72.5,
  score_class = "good",
  source_support = "polygon_estimate"
)
soil_publish_health(soil, run$run_id, scores, "health-kenya-2026-10")

Everybody can read them with soil_health_scores() and count them with soil_health_summary(). At the time of recording no score was published yet:

soil_health_summary(soil)
#> # soilhub soil-health summary: 0 scores on 0 horizons of 0 features

Jobs (soil:publish)

Large publications and source datasets run as jobs on the server. The functions follow them for you; to look at a job yourself:

job <- soil_job(soil, "0b4e...")         # its status now
job <- soil_job_wait(soil, "0b4e...")    # wait until it ends
soil_job_cancel(soil, "0b4e...")         # stop it

A new source dataset (soil:publish)

soil_publish_source() uploads a whole new dataset: a description (the manifest), the places (an sf object with a source_record_id column) and optionally profiles, components, horizons and observations. The server also needs the capability source_ingest. A short example with two profiles:

library(sf)
sites <- st_as_sf(
  data.frame(source_record_id = c("P1", "P2"), x = c(500100, 501200), y = c(4520300, 4521900)),
  coords = c("x", "y"), crs = 32633
)
manifest <- list(
  provider_code = "unina", provider_name = "University of Naples Federico II",
  dataset_code = "campania_profiles", dataset_name = "Campania soil profiles",
  release_code = "2026-10", support_type = "observed_point_profile",
  default_geometry_kind = "POINT", licence_text = "CC-BY 4.0"
)
profiles <- data.frame(source_record_id = c("P1", "P2"), feature_source_id = c("P1", "P2"))
components <- data.frame(source_record_id = c("P1", "P2"), profile_source_id = c("P1", "P2"))
horizons <- data.frame(
  source_record_id = c("P1-1", "P2-1"), component_source_id = c("P1", "P2"),
  top_depth_cm = 0, bottom_depth_cm = 30
)
observations <- data.frame(
  source_record_id = c("P1-1-orgc", "P2-1-orgc"), horizon_source_id = c("P1-1", "P2-1"),
  property_code = "orgc", value = c(12.1, 8.4), unit = "g/kg", status = "observed"
)
ingest <- soil_publish_source(
  soil, manifest, sites, profiles, components, horizons, observations,
  idempotency_key = "campania-2026-10"
)
ingest$release_id

The package writes the bundle file, uploads it with its checksum, asks the server to validate it and then to make it public (promote), and waits for the end. soil_source_validate() and soil_source_promote() do the two steps separately when you want to check before publishing.

Country statistics (soil:admin)

The counts per country (soil_countries()) are refreshed daily. An administrator can ask for a refresh at once:

soil_refresh_countries(soil)
